preamble: Voicing of the voiceless bilabial fricative [ɸ] to [β]. Under Verner's law, the Proto-Germanic *ɸ (written *f) that Grimm's law produced from Proto-Indo-European *p became *β (written *b) when the preceding vowel was unaccented. Wikipedia traces *ubiri 'over' through the stages *upéri > *uféri > *ubéri; Proto-Germanic *sebun 'seven' continues PIE *septḿ̥, which was accented on its final syllable.

examples.note: Stages as given by Wikipedia (Proto-Germanic language): *upéri > *uféri > *ubéri > *ubiri.

examples.from: Pre-Germanic *sepḿ̥t 'seven' (accent on the final syllable, as in PIE *septḿ̥), with *p > *ɸ by Grimm's law
examples.note: Wiktionary derives *sebun from earlier *sebunt and Pre-Germanic *sepḿ̥t, a dissimilatory alteration of *septḿ̥t.
